title: CompMarkGS: Robust Watermarking for Compressed 3D Gaussian Splatting
topic: Social Aspects->Fairness, Equity, Justice and Safety
claim: A protected asset is watermarked, compressed and deployed, then a decoder recovers the hidden message even after distortions to images or the model.
layout: 2 shaded panels, left-to-right, return arrow loops below to verification
description: A wide, two-region flow diagram. The left blue panel, 'Training 3DGS & Embedding Watermark', starts with a black point cloud of a bulldozer scene labeled Initial Points. An arrow leads through a Training box, which also receives a binary key '1011011…' from below. The output is a yellow Watermarked 3DGS with a red-boxed key icon. This passes through a light-green Compression box to a blue Compressed 3DGS, also with a key. A dashed arrow marked Deploy leads right to a pink panel, 'Malicious Use & Identification'. There a globe/browser icon branches into two dashed red groups: Image Distortion (Crop, JPEG, Brightness) and Model Distortion (Prune, Clone, Color), each shown as small bulldozer renders. Both merge into a Watermark Decoder box, which outputs a key. A long arrow returns along the bottom to a green 'Successful Identification' box, where the key is compared with the original.
caption: Application scenario of CompMarkGS. Owners embed the watermark into a 3DGS asset using our proposed method, then compress and distribute the model across various digital environments. The owner can extract the hidden message to verify ownership even if an unauthorized user alters the distributed model or its rendered images.
abstract: As 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is increasingly adopted in various academic and commercial applications due to its high-quality and real-time rendering capabilities, the need for copyright protection is growing. At the same time, its large model size requires efficient compression for storage and transmission. However, compression techniques, especially quantization-based methods, degrade the integrity of existing 3DGS watermarking methods, thus creating the need for a novel methodology that is robust against compression. To ensure reliable watermark detection under compression, we propose a compression-tolerant 3DGS watermarking method that preserves watermark integrity and rendering quality. Our approach utilizes an anchor-based 3DGS, embedding the watermark into anchor attributes, particularly the anchor feature, to enhance security and rendering quality. We also propose a quantization distortion layer that injects quantization noise during training, preserving the watermark after quantization-based compression. Moreover, we employ a frequency-aware anchor growing strategy that enhances rendering quality by effectively identifying Gaussians in high-frequency regions, and an HSV loss to mitigate color artifacts for further rendering quality improvement. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our proposed method preserves the watermark even under compression and maintains high rendering quality.
